events.text: The probe ran and 4 checks failed, so I'm looking at which ones and why.

events.name: Bash
events.head: List failing probe checks
events.input: $ CENTRE=http://127.0.0.1:8960 SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8882 node scripts/probe-tantra-reminders.mjs 2>&1 | grep -E "^FAIL" ; CENTRE=x node -e 1; echo; grep -c "^PASS" <(CENTRE=http://127.0.0.1:8960 SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8882 node scripts/probe-tantra-reminders.mjs 2>&1)

events.name: Bash
events.head: Locate failing assertions
events.input: $ grep -nE "private calendar link and their centre|plan_url \(their own|calendar_url is the new|plan link, rendered" scripts/probe-tantra-reminders.mjs

events.name: Bash
events.head: Compare sim contact links to expected

events.name: Bash
events.head: Find centre base-URL variable
events.input: $ cd /Users/adithyamurali/tantra-redesign/cloud && grep -nE "growthcluborg\.workers\.dev" wrangler.jsonc | head -3; grep -rnoE "env\.[A-Z_]*(URL|ORIGIN|BASE)[A-Z_]*" src/reminders.ts src/calendar.ts | sort -u | head

events.text: My local centre was missing `PUBLIC_URL`, so its links pointed at production while the probe expected local ones. Restarting it with the local URL.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Restart local centre with local URL and rerun probe
events.input: $ kill 60653; /bin/sleep 3; pgrep -f "port 8960" | head -3; (npx wrangler dev --port 8960 --var SIM_URL:http://127.0.0.1:8882 --var PUBLIC_URL:http://127.0.0.1:8960 --persist-to /tmp/t234-wr >/tmp/t234-wr.log 2>&1 & echo WR $!); for i in $(seq 1 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8960/ && break; /bin/sleep 2; done; cd ../app && CENTRE=http://127.0.0.1:8960 SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8882 node scripts/probe-tantra-reminders.mjs > /tmp/t234-probe.log 2>&1; echo exit $?; grep -c "^PASS" /tmp/t234-probe.log; grep -E "^FAIL|FAILED|passed" /tmp/t234-probe.log | head

events.text: The probe now passes all 92 checks (exit 0). Stopping the servers I started.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Stop the local servers by PID
events.input: $ for p in 61564 60651; do pkids=$(pgrep -P $p); kill $p $pkids 2>/dev/null; done; /bin/sleep 2; for p in $(pgrep -f "wrangler dev --port 8960"); do kill $p; done; curl -s -m 2 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8960/ ; curl -s -m 2 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8882/

events.text:
T-234 stays blocked. Nothing had to change for this update: the "waiting on the API key" ask was already cleared, and T-123's go-live owns the live campaigns and the test send. I re-ran the reminders probe today and it passes all 92 checks.

- **Clear the waiting-on for the key:** Done. It says "The API key is already saved in Admin" and asks only for the mailbox, which I confirmed on the board this run.
- **Note that T-123 runs the live campaigns and test send:** Done. It's in today's T-234 board note.
- **Log the evidence on T-123:** Not done. I only updated T-234, so nothing new went onto T-123 this run.
- **Probe passes against the simulator (first done_when item):** Done. All 92 checks pass, exit 0. It first failed 4 checks because the local centre I started was building links with the production address. Restarted with the local address, it passed. No code changed.
- **Live test send in production (second done_when item):** Blocked. team@growthclub.org is not a connected mailbox in the GrowthClub Tantra workspace.
- **Admin shows the four campaign ids and the last import per attendee (third done_when item):** Checked by the probe on the local copy. The production view stays empty until the live campaigns can be created.
- **Status and note:** T-234 set to blocked and note R-b27534cd acknowledged. No files changed, so there was nothing to commit, and I stopped both servers I started.

**Needed from Adi:** connect team@growthclub.org as a mailbox at https://app.usetantra.com (Email Accounts, Connect account). It's the same ask as T-123.

T-123's board entry also asks Adi to rotate the Tantra key, because the one he pasted ended up in the public board mirror's history.
